title: Trombone lessons and uncle Chester Morrison's drum set
summary: He briefly took trombone on a neighbour's instrument, but stayed with drums; an uncle bought his first real set.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Did you ever go ahead and take any lessons on any instrument later with a regular teacher?

Well, Mr. Bill, I did take lessons to play tramo on. But I got back on my drums. I liked it in my drums. This is in Morgan City? Yeah, in Morgan City. But I liked it in my drums and I just went on back and it's on my drums. I didn't stay off them that long. And I had an uncle in the country by the name of Chester Morrison. He bought my first set of drums for me.

And at that time they were really nice drums and I just thought the world of him for buying me a set of drums because I had none. And I kept those drums quite a while until after I made up my mind to come in the arms. Well now did you get your trambone before your set of drums? Well I got the trambone after. I got the drums first. You know old times drums were made. Then I liked it the way trambone, the fellow was playing trambone used to live beside me right next door to me. And I liked the way he used to play and I told him I wanted to play trambone. And I tried to play that. Which I imagine if I'd have stayed on it I'd have been a trambone player.
That was his trambone you were using? Yeah that was his. I never owned none. Well that explains why you sometimes pick up the trambone in Thomas' band. That's right. That's right.
We haven't seen you do that for about a year now. I forgot about it.
That's right. That's right. Well then after you'd borrowed this Foller's trambone it was after that that you got this Chester, did you say Chester Morris?
Chester Morris, that's right. Got you the drums? Yeah he bought a set of drums for me.
